fix_commit_message:
avcodec/hevc/sei: prevent storing a potentially bogus num_ref_displays value in HEVCSEITDRDI

Fixes: 439711052/clusterfuzz-testcase-minimized-ffmpeg_AV_CODEC_ID_HEVC_fuzzer-4956250308935680
Fixes: out of array access

Found-by: continuous fuzzing process https://github.com/google/oss-fuzz/tree/master/projects/ffmpeg
Signed-off-by: James Almer <jamrial@gmail.com>
agent_reasoning: Merged diff composed mechanically by cherry-picking fix d448d6d1a0a4 on top of intro efa9d3deca30 via git's 3-way merge. Vulnerability (IntegerOverflow): The HEVC SEI parser's newly added decode_nal_sei_3d_reference_displays_info() function reads an Exp-Golomb-coded value from the bitstream and stores it directly into the uint8_t field HEVCSEITDRDI.num_ref_displays. Because get_ue_golomb() returns an unsigned int that can be far larger than 255, the assignment truncates the value to 8 bits before the subsequent bounds check ('> 31') is applied. A carefully crafted value can therefore bypass the intended range validation, causing num_ref_displays (after the '+= 1') to end up larger than 31 - the fixed size of all the per-display arrays in the HEVCSEITDRDI struct. The following loop then indexes those fixed-size 31-element arrays with an out-of-range index, resulting in out-of-bounds reads/writes. Root cause: The unsigned value decoded from the bitstream via get_ue_golomb() was stored into a narrow uint8_t struct field before validating it, so the validation check operated on an already-truncated (wrapped) value instead of the original decoded value, defeating the intended upper-bound check of 31.
